name: halibut
desc: Yet another free document preparation system
why: Sgt. Tatham's document system with its own markup language, an idiosyncratic one-off worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Halibut is a documentation production system, a free tool for writing manuals in its own markup language. It reads one source format and produces several output formats from the same text: plain ASCII, HTML, PDF, PostScript, Unix man pages, Unix info (.info files directly), and Windows HTML Help (.CHM) and WinHelp (.HLP) files without a separate help compiler. It is primarily aimed at people producing software manuals.
brief.why_it_exists: Halibut's author, Simon Tatham, wrote it because TeX targets printed pages, TeXinfo's output was not to his taste, debiandoc-sgml lacked the indexing support he wanted, and he disliked DocBook's verbose angle-bracket syntax. It grew out of his work on NASM, where he needed documentation on the web as well as in printable and online formats.
brief.how_it_works: Source is written in a TeX-like backslash-and-braces markup, for example \i{this wrapper} to add a word to the index and \u00F6{oe} for Unicode with a fallback representation. Each output format supplies its own configuration directives, which tailor things like HTML headers, style sheets, and site links. The HTML and PDF outputs carry hyperlinks for every cross-reference, including the index and contents.

commands_seen.context: Gets the latest development sources from the git repository; --recursive is needed because the project uses git submodules.

brief.install_notes: Release source is halibut-1.3.tar.gz, which builds as portable ANSI C. The page says it needs at least a 32-bit platform. Windows users can download a prebuilt Windows executable. For development sources, use git clone with --recursive so submodules are included. Nothing on the page mentions brew-specific steps.
brief.standout: Unlike TeX-derived tools, Halibut is built to emit many output formats directly, including Windows HTML Help and WinHelp, rather than going through TeX or a post-processor. Its indexing system, with merged entries, duplicated entries, and rewritten index styles, is designed in from the start rather than bolted on.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the page shows. Release 1.3 came out 2021-10-30, and the homepage was last modified on the same date. The page does not mention anything newer, so the maintenance level after 2021 is unclear.
brief.caveats: The source is portable C but needs at least a 32-bit platform. The author notes PDF output may have trouble on VMS because of file typing. Windows HTML Help and WinHelp output are old-style Windows formats. The author describes the name as being for 'Historical reasons', and the page gives no licence information. The brew caveats field is empty.
quotes: Halibut is a documentation production system, with elements similar to TeX, debiandoc-sgml, TeXinfo, and others.
It is primarily targeted at people producing software manuals.
Halibut 1.3 was released on 2021-10-30, and supports all of the features described above.
Historical reasons. It's probably better not to ask.
